result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the false belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another and from the natural world. This shift would dissolve the roots of conflict, exploitation, and indifference, revealing the interconnectedness of all life. Without the delusion of "us vs. them," systems of oppression, environmental destruction, and greed would collapse under the weight of their own absurdity. People would act not out of fear or scarcity, but from a deep recognition of shared existence.

Of course, this isn’t a magical fix—it wouldn’t erase complexity or struggle—but it would strip away the narratives that justify harm. The world wouldn’t become perfect, but it would become *honest*. And from there, everything else might follow.
